reason: The cited evidence shows Al reduces density and can increase specific strength in other RHEAs (E2), but it does not address Al solubility in the HfMoTaTiZr system, the retention of a single-phase BCC structure, or the preservation of high-temperature strength. E1 discusses elemental effects in related alloys but provides no data on Al additions. Thus, the key premises about phase stability and strength retention in this specific alloy lack direct support.
premises: Al can dissolve into a BCC lattice and cause lattice distortion without forming deleterious intermetallic phases in HfMoTaTiZr
Partial Al substitution for Hf will reduce density while retaining a single-phase BCC structure
The resulting solid-solution strengthening from Al will preserve high yield strength at room temperature and 1000 °C
A ~10% density reduction and ≤10% strength loss are simultaneously achievable
